title: Operational Uptime Coalition - Campaign Outline and 8-Week Sprint Plan
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, tactical plan for the Operational Uptime Coalition — a cross-functional campaign to raise service availability and SLO ownership maturity across the product surface. The goal is to standardize SLO definitions, improve detection-to-resolution time on latency/availability incidents, and ship a set of light-weight automation and runbook changes that measurably reduce P99/P95 latency tail and reduce SEV count by 20% across targeted services within 8 weeks.

Why this campaign now:
- Several services have experienced increased latency tail after a model rollout and a configuration change in the routing layer.
- We lack a consistent cross-team SLO taxonomy: product SLOs, infra SLOs, customer-facing SLOs are inconsistently defined and measured.
- Quick wins exist: alert noise, missing runbook steps, and routing fallbacks.

Scope (in/out):
- In scope: frontline services for hosting/edge routing, key model inference endpoints, per-route SLO definitions, alerting refinement, runbook standardization, and a small set of automations (rollback on error-rate spike, KV-prefetch warming).
- Out of scope: full infra re-architecture, long-term capacity buys, large model quantization changes (addressed by Optimize later).

Success metrics (quantitative):
- SEV incidents impacting customer-facing latency reduced by 20% in 8 weeks (baseline: last 90 days).
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for latency anomalies improved by 30%.
- Runbook coverage for critical routes increased from 55% to 90%.
- SLO ownership assigned (owner + secondary) for 100% of primary routes.
- One post-deploy canary rollback automation across 3 services deployed and validated.

Roles & RACI (coalition core):
- Campaign lead (Aisha Patel) — overall coordination, reporting, exec sync.
- SRE leads (Miguel Santos, Tom Becker) — runbook standard templates, alert tuning, automation shepherd.
- Product SLO liaison (Priya Rao) — owner alignment, product acceptance criteria, canary policy definitions.
- Observability (Lena Wong) — dashboards, synthetic checks, MTTD instrumentation.
- Solutions / PS (Rachel Kim) — customer-impact assessment, support playbooks.
- Engineering deputies (per-service) — implement changes, PR owners.

8-Week Tactical Sprint Plan (high-level):
Week 0 (prep, pre-campaign):
- Kickoff + alignment doc sent to stakeholders.
- Inventory: export list of top 40 routes by traffic and error budget consumption.
- Baseline dashboards created (availability, p95/p99, error-rate).
Deliverable: campaign dashboard and inventory CSV.

Weeks 1-2 (SLO standardization & quick triage):
- Workshop: SLO taxonomy session with product + infra + SRE, produce canonical SLO template (objective, measurement window, SLI source, owner).
- Assign owners for top 20 routes.
- Alert triage: suppress/eliminate 30% of noisy alerts on routes in scope.
Deliverable: canonical SLO template doc, owner roster, alert-action list.

Weeks 3-4 (Runbooks, synthetic checks, and rollback automation):
- Implement runbook template across top 10 routes; include detection, triage checklist, mitigation commands, escalation map.
- Ship synthetic transaction checks for critical user flows with 1m cadence and latency buckets.
- Prototype simple rollback automation triggered by error-rate threshold (safe fences + PR review).
Deliverable: runbook folder, synthetic-check dashboards, rollback prototype PR.

Weeks 5-6 (Validation, canary policy, and chaos-lite):
- Validate rollback in staging and one low-traffic production cohort; run tabletop exercises.
- Implement canary routing policy for two services (10% traffic for canary with auto-fallback).
- Run low-blast chaos tests (network latency injection) to validate detection and rollback path.
Deliverable: canary policy config, test logs, tabletop exercise notes.

Weeks 7-8 (Measurement, handoff, and post-mortem):
- Measure KPIs vs baseline, collect feedback, finalize permanent runbooks and handoff to service owners for ongoing stewardship.
- Prepare executive one-pager for leadership with outcomes and recommended follow-ups (Optimize, Dedicated capacity proposals).
Deliverable: campaign report, updated runbook index, next-steps backlog.

Communication & Cadence:
- Weekly coalition sync (30m) — Mon 09:30 PT, 8-week campaign. Notes posted in shared drive.
- Asynchronous updates: Slack channel #uptime-coalition with thread summary daily.
- Exec sync: biweekly 15m checkpoint with Director SRE and Head of Product.

Key decisions & guardrails:
- Any rollback automation must require a kill-switch and manual override.
- Canary policy must include traffic percentage caps and safety windows (no global rollout without signoff).
- SLO changes impacting billing or contractual SLAs require Product + Legal review (outside this campaign scope, will surface flags).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Runbook adoption stalls because service teams busy with feature launches.
  Mitigation: Provide one-hour pairing sessions and small PR templates to reduce lift.
- Risk: Synthetic checks create noise if poorly designed.
  Mitigation: Observe for 48h in staging and tune thresholds before prod enable.
- Risk: Automation causes unintended rollbacks.
  Mitigation: Start with a read-only dry-run, then gated rollout with staged ramp.

Dependencies & blockers:
- Observability team needs access to model-serving telemetry (KV cache hit rates, sequence length histograms).
- Networking team must approve canary routing changes (expected 2-week lead).
- Product teams must commit a secondary owner per route within Week 2.

Checklist (minimum deliverables):
- [ ] SLO template created and approved.
- [ ] Owner roster for top 20 routes.
- [ ] Runbook template and first 10 completed.
- [ ] Synthetic checks for top 5 flows.
- [ ] Rollback automation prototype merged and tested.
- [ ] Canary policy validated in one service.
- [ ] Campaign report and exec one-pager completed.

Evaluation & next steps after campaign:
- If KPIs met: expand coalition to next 20 routes and propose an Optimize project to tune batching/caching parameters as part of cost/perf reductions.
- If KPIs partially met: run a 4-week remediation sprint focused on the highest-impact gaps (alerts or ownership).
- If KPIs not met: convene root-cause retro, escalate blockers (capacity, infra limits) and recommend Dedicated capacity trial for hotspot services.

Appendix (links & notes):
- Inventory export location: drive:shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/uptime-coalition/inventory-2026-01-12.csv
- SLO template draft: drive:shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/uptime-coalition/slo-template-v1.docx
- Quick reference runbook template: drive:shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/runbooks/template-runbook.md
- Related Linear issues: SRE-4823 (alert-reduction), SRE-4899 (canary-policy), ENG-5510 (rollback-automation-PR).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep campaign focused on measurable impact; avoid creeping into full-scale infra changes.
- Pair with product owners early — ownership is the single biggest friction point historically.
- Capture one or two “hero case studies” (before/after) to sell momentum across org.

End.
